text: main goal package facilitate research climate shocks providing functions support different stages working climate data. download_inmet function downloads ZIP files containing data INMET weather stations Brazilian government’s website. build_inmet_dataset helps users create partitioned database INMET data, read_inmet provides access database. Functions nearest_station kriging_inmet connect municipalities INMET database, allowing researchers match climate data information sources, IBGE TSE. makes possible conduct correlations forms statistical analysis. vignette demonstrates central functions working climateBR. hope enjoy ride.

title: Spatial Interpolation Using Ordinary Kriging
text: Spatial interpolation commonly used estimate meteorological variables locations direct observations available. kriging_inmet() function implements ordinary kriging using weather station observations spatial prediction locations provided sf objects. vignette demonstrates interpolate accumulated rainfall INMET weather stations.
code: library(climateBR) library(dplyr) library(sf) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork)

title: Spatial Interpolation Using Ordinary Kriging
text: example uses rainfall observations 2024 Rio Grande Sul flood event together municipality geometries. station observations converted sf object projected planar coordinate reference system suitable distance-based spatial analysis.
code: data("floods_rs") data("mun_stations")  # Alternative for: geobr::read_municipality(year = 2024) tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".rda") on.exit(unlink(tmp), add = TRUE)  download.file(   "https://github.com/kaiorb52/dados_municipais/raw/main/mun_24.rda",   destfile = tmp,   mode = "wb" )  load(tmp) rain_sf <- floods_rs |>   st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>   st_transform(crs = 29193)  mun_centroid <- mun_24 |>   select(code_muni, geom) |>   mutate(     ponto = st_point_on_surface(geom)   ) |>   st_drop_geometry()  mun_grid_sf <- mun_centroid |>   st_as_sf() |>   st_transform(crs = 29193)

title: Spatial Interpolation Using Ordinary Kriging
text: kriging_inmet() function computes empirical variogram, fits spherical variogram model, performs ordinary kriging predictions target locations. predicted values (var1.pred) prediction variances (var1.var) attached municipality dataset.
code: krig_result <- kriging_inmet(   stations_df = rain_sf,   mun_geo     = mun_grid_sf ) #> [using ordinary kriging] mun_pred <- mun_centroid |>   select(code_muni) |>   bind_cols(     krig_result |>       st_drop_geometry() |>       select(         precip_krig     = var1.pred,         precip_krig_var = var1.var       )   )

title: Spatial Interpolation Using Ordinary Kriging
text: following map displays municipality-level rainfall estimates obtained ordinary kriging.
code: p1 <- mun_24 |>   left_join(mun_pred, by = "code_muni") |>   ggplot() +   geom_sf(aes(fill = precip_krig), color = NA) +   labs(title = "Ordinary Kriging") +   scale_fill_distiller(     palette = "RdYlGn",     direction = 1,     na.value = "grey80"   ) +   theme_void() +   theme(     legend.position = c(0.9, 0.1)   )

title: Spatial Interpolation Using Ordinary Kriging
text: comparison, map assigns municipality rainfall value closest weather station. figure compares rainfall estimates generated using ordinary kriging values obtained nearest-station approach.  Ordinary kriging generally produces smoother spatial surfaces incorporates information multiple nearby stations, whereas nearest-station method assigns value municipalities linked given station may introduce abrupt spatial discontinuities. approach important advantages limitations. Ordinary kriging accounts spatial dependence usually generates realistic spatial patterns others methods. However, statistical interpolation technique, may produce physically unrealistic estimates, negative rainfall values, often smooths spatial field, reducing magnitude extreme precipitation events. result, high observed rainfall totals may underestimated interpolated surface. contrast, nearest-station approach preserves original observed values, including extremes, can create large areas identical rainfall estimates multiple municipalities may assigned station. can lead artificial boundaries abrupt changes neighboring municipalities reflect continuous nature precipitation processes.
code: mun_floods <- floods_rs |>   left_join(     mun_stations |>       filter(station_order == 1),     by = c("code_wmo" = "code_wmo")   )  p2 <- mun_24 |>   left_join(     mun_floods |>       select(code_ibge7, total_rainfall),     by = c("code_muni" = "code_ibge7")   ) |>   ggplot() +   geom_sf(aes(fill = total_rainfall), color = NA) +   labs(title = "Nearest Station") +   scale_fill_distiller(     palette = "RdYlGn",     direction = 1,     na.value = "grey80"   ) +   theme_void() +   theme(     legend.position = c(0.9, 0.1)   )

title: Download Rainfall, Temperature, and Wind Data from Brazil
text: climateBR, can download historical INMET data using download_inmet() function, specifying one years. downloaded raw station CSV files can processed partitioned Apache Arrow dataset using build_inmet_dataset(). Finally, read_inmet() can used query processed dataset. package also provides datasets containing information nearest INMET stations municipality Brazil.
code: library(climateBR)  download_inmet(   years = 2026,   unzip_to = "data/raw/inmet" )  build_inmet_dataset(   input = "data/raw/inmet/",   output = "data/processed/inmet/" )  df_inmet <- read_inmet(path = "data/processed/inmet") data("mun_stations") # The `mun_stations` dataset was created using the `nearest_stations()` function and contains the five nearest stations for each municipality.  temp_rj <- df_inmet |>    group_by(ano, mes, codigo_wmo) |>    summarise(     temp_max = max(       temperatura_maxima_na_hora_ant_aut_c,       na.rm = TRUE     )   ) |>    left_join(     mun_stations |>        filter(station_order == 1) |>        select(state_muni, code_ibge7, code_wmo),      by = c("codigo_wmo" = "code_wmo")   ) |>    filter(state_muni == "RJ") |>    collect() |>    arrange(-temp_max)    # A tibble: 644 × 6 # # Groups:   ano, mes [7] #      ano   mes codigo_wmo temp_max state_muni code_ibge7 #    <int> <int> <chr>         <dbl> <chr>           <dbl> #  1  2026     1 A601           41   RJ            3305554 #  2  2026     1 A601           41   RJ            3304144 #  3  2026     1 A601           41   RJ            3303609 #  4  2026     1 A601           41   RJ            3302270 #  5  2026     1 A601           41   RJ            3302007 #  6  2026     1 A621           40.8 RJ            3305109 #  7  2026     1 A621           40.8 RJ            3303500 #  8  2026     1 A621           40.8 RJ            3303203 #  9  2026     1 A621           40.8 RJ            3302858 # 10  2026     1 A621           40.8 RJ            3300456 # # ℹ 634 more rows # # ℹ Use `print(n = ...)` to see more rows library(ggplot)  temp_rj |>    ggplot(aes(x = as.character(mes), y = temp_max)) +   geom_boxplot() +   theme_linedraw() +   labs(y = "Max. Temp (Cº)", x = "Month") +   ylim(20, 40) library(geobr)  mun_24 <- geobr::read_municipality(year = 2024)  mun_rj <- mun_24 |>    filter(abbrev_state == "RJ") |>    select(code_muni, geom)  mun_temp_rj <- mun_rj |>    left_join(     mun_stations |> filter(station_order == 1) |> select(code_ibge7, code_wmo),      by = c("code_muni" = "code_ibge7")   ) |>    left_join(     temp_rj,      by = c("code_wmo" = "codigo_wmo")   )  mun_temp_rj$mes <- factor(   mun_temp_rj$mes,   levels = 1:12,   labels = month.name )  ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = mun_temp_rj, aes(fill = temp_max)) +   scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdYlGn") +   facet_wrap(.~mes) +   labs(fill = "Max. Temp (Cº)") +   theme_void() +   theme(     legend.position = c(0.785, 0.185),     plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white")   )

title: Read INMET meteorological observations — read_inmet
text: Reads INMET dataset previously created [build_inmet_dataset()]. dataset accessed Arrow Dataset interface, allowing efficient filtering without loading observations memory.

title: Read INMET meteorological observations — read_inmet
code: read_inmet(   path = NULL,   years = NULL,   stations = NULL,   variables = NULL,   collect = FALSE )

title: Read INMET meteorological observations — read_inmet
text: path Character. Path directory containing processed INMET dataset. years Integer vector years read. `NULL`, available years returned. stations Character vector WMO station codes. `NULL`, stations returned. variables Character vector variables (columns) return. `NULL`, variables returned. collect Logical. `TRUE`, filtered dataset collected memory data frame. `FALSE` (default), Arrow Dataset query returned.

title: Read INMET meteorological observations — read_inmet
text: `collect = FALSE`, returns Arrow Dataset query. `collect = TRUE`, returns data frame containing selected observations.

title: Read INMET meteorological observations — read_inmet
text: function performs filtering directly disk whenever possible, making suitable working large datasets. Setting `collect = TRUE` loads selected observations memory. may require large amount RAM reading many years stations simultaneously. Consider filtering year, station, variables collecting data.

title: Read INMET meteorological observations — read_inmet
code: # Requires INMET data downloaded with download_inmet() and # processed into an Arrow dataset with build_inmet_dataset(). # See the vignette "climateBR: An R package to download meteorological data from Brazil". # for the complete workflow of this function.  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{  ## Read a single year without loading the data into memory rainfall_df1 <- read_inmet(   path = dataset_dir,   years = 2000,   collect = FALSE )  ## Read multiple years and collect the results into memory rainfall_df2 <- read_inmet(   path = dataset_dir,   years = 2000:2005,   collect = TRUE )  ## For large datasets, keeping collect = FALSE is generally ## recommended to avoid excessive memory usage. } # }

text: inmet_stations — dataset essentially revamped version previous rain_stations dataset. older dataset contained information INMET stations available 2000 2024, meaning station appear multiple times across different years. new version uses recent station information available 2026 contains one observation per station, avoiding unnecessary repetition. mun_stations — previous mun_stations_distance dataset contained distances municipalities INMET stations every two-year period 2008 2024. new version contains distances calculated municipalities INMET stations using inmet_stations dataset nearest_stations function. municipality — brand-new dataset containing basic information Brazilian municipalities, including IBGE TSE municipality codes, state, latitude longitude municipality’s centroid. floods_rs — renamed ‘id_who’ column ‘code_wmo’.
